newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks soft in directionless market.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks soft in directionless market.

text.p: Zimbabwean stocks traded softer in small volumes on Wednesday with brokers saying most market players had taken to the sidelines ahead of some corporate results due in May.
The key industrial index dropped 51.71 points to close at 10,825.82 and brokers said they expected the market to continuing coming off after the Workers' Day break on Thursday.
"Nobody wants to buy shares at the moment. Everybody is just waiting to see the results coming in the next two to four weeks," one broker said.
"Volumes are very small although we were busy in bits and pieces," another one said.

Notable among the day's losers, steel windows and doors manufacturer Radar slid 80 cents to 500, hotel and supermarket group Meikles dropped 70 cents to 2,830, sugar grower Hippo shed 60 cents to 1,600 and publishers Zimpapers lost 50 cents to 5,900.
Minings continuned lustreless on the back of a bearish bullion with Wankie Colliery trading 10 cents off at 540.
The mining index slipped 3.61 points to 1,018.54.
